The pacing of the story feels very natural, deliberate, and well-balanced. The narrative unfolds largely in real-time (or close to it), covering the brief span of a single morning ferry crossing. Rather than compressing large swaths of time, the author uses subtle stretching of time—focusing on minute physical details like a stuck coin in a leather bag, a loose rubber seal, and the slow, sparse dialogue between characters—to mirror the quiet, methodical, and slightly sluggish atmosphere of a foggy morning routine. At the very end, the brief moment of the phone vibrating is stretched across the unloading process and the final lines, effectively building quiet tension and emotional weight as Ilse chooses not to answer the call from "Jonas."
